title: F-star residue (i): mixed anchor-repair-pivot lemma MX, tied-instance certificates, and a tied-domain search (no kappa)
body:
# F-star residue (i): mixed anchor-repair-pivot lemma MX, tied-instance certificates, and a tied-domain search (no kappa)

## Scope

Kappa-blocker **KB5b** (explicit open request; scope changed from the drawn card and recorded in `TASK.json`): residue class **(i) tied-minimum / isotropic lines** of open problem **F-star** of the merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` package (section 7): `cert(M) >= floor(2v/3)` for every exact 3-total rational decoder `M = sum_j p_j q_j^T`. This is the exact residue that [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717) (Aaron Wang) left after proving Lemmas SF, MP, RK and AN: lines the mod-2 anchor cannot anchor (tied-minimum / isotropic lines), where Lemma AN handles only the count of odd diagonals and not their repair or ordering. Package `research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691/`, branch `research/agent-65-fstar-tied-residue-dcc97691`, base main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (priority revision 4). No kappa, certificate, supplier, window or frontier change. **F-star itself is not proved and not refuted here.**

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed).

## Result 1 — Lemma MX (PROVEN)

A mixed anchor-repair-pivot certificate with exact hypotheses, in two order forms. Anchor labels on a set `A` (lines with `M_tt` odd), one-sided repairs `a*(t)` on a set `U` (with `b` fixed at the anchor's `b0`), matched pivots `a(t) = b(t) = e_{c(t)}` with `c(t)` in `D(t)` on the rest `T`; per pivot class `C_i`, `MAS(Z[C_i])` is the maximum acyclic induced subset of the zero digraph. Then `cert(M) >= |A| + |U| + sum_i MAS(Z[C_i])` under either (a-first) "the repairs kill their `A`/`U` and `T` blockers and no `A`-to-`T` conflict remains", or (t-first) "the repairs kill their `A`/`U` blockers and no `T`-to-`A`/`U` conflict remains". Written proof in the README. Its `U`/`T`-empty special case is Lemma AN of [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717); its `A`/`U`-empty special case is Lemma MP of [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717), so MX subsumes both as sufficient conditions.

## Result 2 — the canonical tied instances are closed by structural certificates (CHECKED)

Per-line residue classification (relative to the stored primitive 2-integral normalization: `anchor_good` = `M_tt` odd; `repairable_1s` = full one-sided repair exists with `b` fixed; `tied_isotropic` = neither), then exhaustive maximization over **all** pivot maps as unit masks (4096 on `tied_min`, 6144 on `cex_min_1`), every accepted value carrying a witness replayed by an independent checker:

| instance | v | floor(2v/3) | ceil(2v/3) | AN | MP (exhaustive) | MX (max) | engine witness | PR 2111 recorded |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| tied_min | 12 | 8 | 8 | 0 | 9 | 9 | 11 (re-found) | 11 (recorded) |
| cex_min_1 | 19 | 12 | 13 | 8 | 16 | 16 | 18 (replayed) | 18 (recorded) |

F-star holds on both canonical tied-minimum instances by a structural certificate (9 and 16, at or above both the floor and the ceiling threshold), even though the mod-2 anchor is vacuous on `tied_min` (0 of 12 lines) and short on `cex_min_1` (8 of 19). Both fixtures are entirely `tied_isotropic` outside the anchor set (0 one-sided repairable), so the residue is total there. The engine witnesses reproduce DreamingOfClouds' recorded one-copy L8 maxima of [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) (their CP-SAT optimality is recorded, not re-verified here).

## Result 3 — exact obstruction to the mixed route (CHECKED)

On `cex_min_1` no anchor/pivot mixture helps in either block order: the a-first separation fails for 6144/6144 pivot maps (`A`-to-`T` conflict) and the t-first separation fails for 6144/6144 (`T`-to-`A`/`U` conflict). The winning value 16 is the pure matched-pivot construction. This is the exact obstruction to extending AN/MP by naive mixing on the canonical hard instance.

## Result 4 — tied-domain falsifier search, smallest first (CHECKED, scoped negative)

40 instances at `v = 3..12` (two per family and `v`), families `tied_isotropic` (every line constructed with two tied minimal valuations at level 0 and even diagonal) and `mixed` (half unique-minimum anchorable, half tied). Zero falsifiers. `cert = v` on all 40: 16 decided by exhaustive `a`-enumeration at `v <= 6`, 24 pinned by full-size replayed witnesses (a witness of size `v` pins `cert = v` exactly). Minimum witness ratio 1.0. The falsifier criterion (explicit admissible pairing `B` with block-rank chain cost below `floor(2v/3)`, which by the proven chain would refute F-star) was tested by an exhaustive `B`-scan up to 12 free pairs and a deterministic local search above: no `B` below threshold on any instance (bounded search, not an exhaustive non-falsification proof). Lemma MP reaches `v` on all 40; Lemma MX is never below MP and never strictly above it on this domain.

## What is proved, witnessed, demoted

- **PROVEN:** Lemma MX, both order forms, exact hypotheses, written proof.
- **CHECKED (stdlib `verify.py`, deterministic, certificate digest `439d75261e9a2b9e`):** controls (brute/engine agreement 3/3 at `v = 3`, diagonal decoder `cert = 3`, corrupted-witness rejection 2/2, MX all-anchor reproducing AN's count, MP control with replayed witness); the fixture classification; the exhaustive MP/MX maxima 9/16 with replayed witnesses; the 6144/6144 obstruction counts in both forms; engine witnesses 11/18; the 40-instance search (`cert = v` on all, zero falsifiers).
- **DEMOTED:** F-star for general rational decoders is not proved. That matched pivots always reach `floor(2v/3)` is witnessed on 42 instances, not proved. No hypothesis is claimed necessary. Residue classes (ii) (non-3-dichromatic zero digraphs) and (iii) (non-dyadic entries) are untouched. `B`-scan values are bounded-search upper bounds on the minimum chain cost. The fixture certificates 11/18 rest on [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111)'s recorded CP-SAT optimality. Exact pairing costs elsewhere (12 on `tied_min`, [PR 2379](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2379) by Aaron Wang; 21 on `cex_min_1`, [PR 2206](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2206) by Nick Petalas) are cited, not recomputed.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691
```

Expected: `PASS_FSTARTIED_CONTROLS`, `PASS_FSTARTIED_FIXTURES`, `PASS_FSTARTIED_MX`, `PASS_FSTARTIED_SEARCH`, `PASS_FSTAR_TIED_RESIDUE`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/fstar-tied-residue-seeddcc97691 outcome=completed` (registered replay: 378.81 s, under the 600 s manifest cap). `make` is not installed on the authoring host.

## Credit

F-star, `cert(M)`, L8 labellings and the proven chain: merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` ([PR 1590](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1590) by DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code assistance). Fixtures `tied_min`/`cex_min_1`, their recorded certificate limits and the stored cost-22 pairing: DreamingOfClouds, [PR 2111](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111) and [PR 2162](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162). The residue statement, Lemmas SF/MP/RK/AN and the engine design this adapts: Aaron Wang, [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717). The falsifier-census frontier: Aaron Wang, [PR 2335](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2335). Exact cost 12 of `tied_min`: Aaron Wang, [PR 2379](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2379). Exact cost 21 of `cex_min_1`: Nick Petalas, [PR 2206](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2206). New work here is Lemma MX with its proof, the residue classification, the mixed-route obstruction and the tied-domain search.

**Open next questions** are in the package README: (1) does the matched-pivot family always reach `floor(2v/3)` (which would prove F-star)? (2) does insertion-finite mixing (per-anchor-line cuts of the pivot order) survive the 6144/6144 obstruction? (3) which label patterns do the attaining certificates 11 and 18 actually use?
